mika (infra): Heads-up — cluster autoscaler failing to provision GPU nodes for the new mig/time-slice experiments. Pods are Pending with "0/0 nodes available" even though we have spare GPU quota in region-us-west1.

raj (runtime): seeing same. Pod requests: "nvidia.com/gpu: 1" and label selector "gpu-type: 1g-mig". CA logs show "no template matches".

claire (platform): Did we create a node pool with the exact label and matching instance type? autoscaler needs nodeGroup names and the right resourceLimits.

mika (infra): We created three pools last night:
- gpu-dedicated-usw1 (no-MIG, reserve 1 whole A100 per pod)
- gpu-mig-usw1 (MIG-enabled A100, exposes 7x slices)
- gpu-timeslice-preemptible-usw1 (time-slicing via MPS, preemptible)

sam (eng-sre): Quick checklist: node pool labels, taints/tolerations, CA resourceLimits, and if using GKE, ensure --enable-autoprovisioning or we added pools as managed instance groups. Also check maxnodes/minnodes per pool.

anya (eng-ml): For model-serving latency, MIG 1g slices are great for small embedding models. But large 8k-context chat models need full GPU. We need routing by pod annotation to prefer pool.

autoscaler-bot: [info] scale attempt at 2024-10-15T10:03:12Z: no suitable node group found for pod "model-server-embed-xyz"

raj (runtime): Sharing CA snippet we used (edited for clarity):
```yaml
cluster-autoscaler: 
  expander: least-waste
  balance-similar-node-groups: true
  max-node-provision-time: 10m
  resourceLimits: 
    gpu: 200
```
Problem is the autoscaler only recognizes pools with label "accelerator-type: nvidia-a100" but our MIG pool labels are "gpu-type: 1g-mig". mismatch.

claire (platform): Two options:
1) Teach CA via --node-group-auto-discovery tags or add a custom resourceLimits entry per pool.
2) Use nodeAffinity on pods for exact node pool names.

mika (infra): We tried affinity and it worked for scheduling, but autoscaler still won't scale gpu-mig because CA expects integer accelerator counts on node templates. MIG exposes fractional devices at the kube level.

sam (eng-sre): Right — CA expects requests like "nvidia.com/gpu: 1" which maps to 1 whole device. For MIG we historically expose each slice as a full allocatable device (kubelet with device plugin) but some clouds don't advertise it to CA. Need the node group to advertise the GPU count per instance properly.

anya (eng-ml): Also note time-slicing pool uses MPS and pods request "cpu: 4, memory: 16Gi, gpu-time-slice: 0.2" (we used a custom scheduler). That's not compatible with vanilla CA.

raj (runtime): Proposal: create CA-friendly labels and pseudo-resources. We can add label "ca-gpu-kind: mig-1g" and configure the device plugin to register "nvidia.com/mig-1g: 1" per slice. Then CA resourceLimits/gpu should include these names.

claire (platform): I like that. Steps:
- Update device-plugin config for MIG pool to register distinct resource name (nvidia.com/mig-1g).
- Add node pool metadata tag so CA auto-discovery picks it up.
- Set CA resourceLimits for both "nvidia.com/gpu" (whole) and "nvidia.com/mig-1g" (slices).

mika (infra): Minimal roll plan:
1) Create a small canary gpu-mig-canary pool (3 nodes) with the device-plugin change.
2) Deploy a canary embedding service with nodeSelector gpu-type: 1g-mig.
3) Monitor CA decisions and scale behavior for 24h.

sam (eng-sre): Add config: scale-up delay 1m, scale-down delay 15m, max empty bulk delete 1. We should avoid oscillation with preemptible/time-slice pool.

anya (eng-ml): Cost note: preemptible time-slice pool saves ~60% per hour, but tail latency increases ~20ms on average. For interactive chat models that's bad; for batch embedding runs it's fine. Suggest routing: latency-critical -> gpu-dedicated; small requests -> gpu-mig; bulk -> timeslice-preemptible.

raj (runtime): Also watch pod fragmentation: if pods ask for 1x mig-1g but our scheduler packs them poorly, we get stranded resources. Consider a top-off DaemonSet to keep node tails in good shape or use kube-scheduler plugins for packing.

claire (platform): I'll open a short RFC and runbook: include kubectl commands for ops:
```bash
# list nodes with mig label
kubectl get nodes -l gpu-type=1g-mig -o wide
# show CA logs
kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/cluster-autoscaler
# force scale test
kubectl run -i --rm load-canary --image=busybox --restart=Never -- sleep 100000
```

mika (infra): One more gotcha: regional quota. We had quota available globally, but specific instance types in us-west1-a were exhausted. Need CA to prefer zones with available capacity or fallback to other region pools. Smart routing required.

sam (eng-sre): We'll add a CA expander policy to prefer zones in this order: us-west1-b, us-west1-c, us-west1-a and add fallback to dedicated in eu-west1 if all fail. Also alert when cross-zone scaling happens.

anya (eng-ml): TL;DR: conservative rollout, three logical pools (dedicated, mig, timeslice), CA needs to see MIG resources as separate resource names, and routing layer must pick pool by latency/cost target.

claire (platform): I'll schedule the canary tomorrow 09:00 PT. tagging: @mika @raj @sam @anya. I'll post the RFC link when done. :thumbsup:

mika (infra): Thanks — will be on-call for the first 2h of the canary.

autoscaler-bot: [warn] alert created: "CA_no_matching_nodegroup" - investigate node group discovery and device plugin registration

raj (runtime): If anyone needs the device-plugin patch, ping me. I'll share a patch that registers "nvidia.com/mig-1g" and sets capacity per node based on MIG config.

sam (eng-sre): Nice. Also add a metric for "GPU fragment ratio" so we can track wasted slices over time.

anya (eng-ml): Agreed. Let's reconvene after 24h of canary data.
